exercise.instruction: Write the program: include <map> and <string>. Create std::map<std::string, int> scores; set scores["alice"] = 3 and scores["bob"] = 5, then increment bob with scores["bob"]++. Finally iterate with a range-based for loop printing entry.first << ": " << entry.second on its own line.
hints: Hint 1: std::map<std::string, int> scores; scores["alice"] = 3; scores["bob"] = 5;
Hint 3: for (const auto& entry : scores) { std::cout << entry.first << ": " << entry.second << std::endl; }

quiz.question: How does std::map order its keys?
What is each entry in a map?
Why might operator[] be wrong for existence checks?
options: It inserts a default value when the key is missing
It only works for string keys
